# 1.2.73 - a body is found once, a chapter ends once, a reset takes the tokens

The twentieth stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E11), released on its own: the
discovery of a body, the end of a chapter and the season reset. A body is
announced once, by the primary GM's browser, and the hold it leaves says what
is true. The chapter's end is one ordered list that counts once. Edit campaign
asks before it moves a chapter or opens a trial. The season reset runs in a
fixed order, removes every project token and asks where the cast's tokens go.
Most of it was measured in the headless harness, some only read in the code,
and none of it has been tried at a table.

## Before installing

1. **Every browser at the table should run 1.2.73.** The gather after a
   discovery now sends a packet that moves each player's camera to their own
   token (the harness reads the call, not a camera). A browser on 1.2.72
   ignores it (read in the code: unknown kinds are ignored), so that screen
   stays where it was.
2. **The first load sweeps the project tokens old seasons left.** Once, on the
   primary GM's browser, over every scene, it removes the tokens of projects
   that no longer exist and tells the GM: "{n} project tokens were left on the
   map by projects that no longer exist, and have been removed." A second token
   of a project that exists is only warned about. Not tried at a table yet
   (LIVE-E11-06).
3. **The reset window has 28 groups, not 29.** "The notes the cast wrote on
   their own sheets" is gone: a Daggerheart character has no notes field (read
   at Daggerheart 2.6.5), so the tick wiped nothing. A table that had unticked
   it forgets that choice.
4. **A macro may need changing.** `game.drpg.discoverBody` and
   `game.drpg.applyChapterEnd` do nothing on a GM who is not the primary and
   tell that GM whom to ask.
5. **Settings and texts.** Nothing new in the settings window; one hidden world
   setting, `bodiesFound` (120 registrations in `settings.mjs`, 119 at 1.2.72),
   and one new clause in `migrate.mjs`, the sweep above. `lang/en.json` gains
   65 strings, loses 9 and rewords 20 (3158 to 3214); `lang/pl.json` gains 77,
   loses 13 and changes 24 (3897 to 3961). The handbooks (GM and player,
   English and Polish) were updated for these changes.

## At the table

### The discovery of a body

- **A body is found once, by the primary GM's browser** (on another GM's, "A
  body is discovered" announces nothing and names whom to ask). The module
  records which bodies were found, per chapter and season. A verdict, the end
  of a trial or a walk past the body later does not announce it again, and its
  card stays up through the Investigation. An execution, a verdict's or the
  Final Trial's, is never a body to find. A dead student's token no longer
  counts as one of the two who find a body; a Monocub still does.
- **The order.** It publishes every kept death of a body in that room, gathers
  everyone, posts the card with its sound, pauses the music (by default; read
  in the code) and holds. Only then does the GM get the Prep question, "Body
  found in {room}", about this chapter's Faint Prep traces.
- **The GM's window** marks a body already announced this chapter, "{name}
  (announced this chapter)", and refuses to announce it by name again. A death
  that could not be made known is not named, and the GMs are whispered to make
  it known in the Players window.

### The hold

- **The words** say the Investigation has not started yet, not that everything
  has stopped. Actions stay open: only the Eclipse waits, and its chevron is
  marked disabled with the reason on it ("A body has been found - start the
  Investigation first."; how it looks is not seen). In the Class Trial actions
  are held as before.
- **The hold is loud only in its own hour,** and a body announced once the
  Investigation has started holds no Eclipse. The Next line names a body nobody
  has found; after the announcement it names the Key Remnants not on the map
  yet, then in the Investigation the autopsy if it was not issued this chapter.

### The chapter's end

- **The primary GM ends it;** another GM is told whom to ask. The window keeps
  the chapter, session, day and phase it was opened on; if any has moved,
  nothing is done and the GMs are told to open it again.
- **One ordered list of nine steps.** A step that fails is named and the rest
  still run, except the next morning, which waits when closing the trial
  failed. The phase is read before each step: if something else has moved it
  (measured with a Class Trial another GM opens), the end stops there, what
  ran stays done, and the GMs are told which of the steps asked for did not
  run. Moving the chapter or the session on from the Investigation puts the
  clock back in Daily Life.
- **The window offers what it can do:** the reveal box is unticked and greyed
  when there is nothing to reveal (the greying is not seen), and a warning
  names who holds the Truth Bullets with no real type recorded.

### Edit campaign

- **A chapter change asks first:** "This corrects the chapter number only - no
  reveal, no sweep, no Blackened. End a chapter with End the chapter. Cancel
  keeps the chapter and applies the rest." Moving into the Class Trial asks
  too. A correction of the hour calls off a called assembly, in a card the
  table sees; moving the time of day on keeps it.

### The season reset

- **The window's list of what goes follows the ticks** (a group left unticked
  is struck through), and the groups run in one order, the incident first. A
  running incident is abandoned, not closed: nobody is killed or put on the
  Blackened register, no tool breaks, no close card goes to its players.
- **Each group takes what its label says:** Health and Sanity whole again, each
  bedroom's key handed back, a Level Up's experiences removed, every Call armed
  for a roll cleared, every hidden stash opened, every project token on every
  scene removed. A starting sheet kept before 1.2.73 cannot tell a Level Up's
  experience from the GM's own; the handbook says which go, and the report
  names the ones left.
- **Where the cast's tokens go,** three choices: they stay where they stand
  (the default, not remembered), each student to their own bedroom as Room
  Setup assigns it, or everyone to one room. A student with no bedroom, no
  token on that map, or a token on another map than the room stays and is named
  in the report. A body stays where it fell.
- **A failed step is told:** "The reset did not finish: {groups}. Everything
  else went. Run the reset again with only those ticked." RESET must be typed
  in capitals. A GM with a lower id connecting while the reset runs stops it
  before its next step: what ran stays done, and the error and the report name
  what did not run and the primary GM.
- **Last season's records** (Remnants, motive, Final Truth, the autopsy, a
  Monocub's silence) carry their season, so after a reset last season's Chapter
  1 is not read as this one.

### Project tokens, and two GMs

- The primary GM's browser keeps project tokens in step. A token deleted by
  hand stays deleted until **Show on the map** in the manager puts it back; a
  token of no live project goes whenever the primary's map is drawn; a second
  GM's draw places nothing. Two people at two screens is LIVE-E11-09.

## Changed

- **The stamp.** `bodiesFound`, a world setting keyed `<epoch>:<chapter>` with
  one writer (`announceBody`, R349); a death record carries its phase, season
  and a random `deathId`; `bodiesToDiscover` (R347) reads them and
  `witnessesOf` (R348) leaves out the dead.
- **Two ordered lists:** `CHAPTER_END_STEPS` (nine steps) and `RESET_STEPS` (29
  keys: the 28 groups and `placeCast`). `sameSeason` reads an `epoch` on traces
  and the motive. New: the clock's `trialEndedAt`, the GM flag
  `levelUpExperiences` and the `SYNC.gather` packet.
- **Project tokens:** `projectOwning`, a `deleteToken` hook and
  `sweepProjectTokens` in `projects-map.mjs`; the clause
  `sweepOldProjectTokens`.
- **New tests:** R346 to R358 and R375 to R378 (13 in tier 0 and 4 in tier 1;
  R359 to R374 were never used; next free R379), 48 new tier-2 tests, and the
  ci scenario 65-season (21 scenarios in the ci set, 20 at 1.2.72).
- **Unchanged:** the GM bridge and the relay guard (neither file is in the
  stage's diff), and the manifest's Foundry and Daggerheart versions. The stage
  registry gains E76 (planned 1.2.118); E57 to E59 move one release on.

## Known gaps

- Nine live checks stand open, items 154 to 162 of the audit's section 9.2
  (LIVE-E11-01 to 09): what a player's canvas draws after a reset or a sweep,
  the cameras panning, the dimmed Eclipse chevron, the End of chapter window's
  disabled boxes, and two GMs at two screens. The harness reads documents and
  attributes, not the canvas or the layout.
- The reset moves the cast with Foundry's `region.teleportTokens`; the harness
  has none, so only the fallback ran (LIVE-E11-07). With *Deaths and Monocubs*
  unticked a moved token could enter a body's room (not measured).
- Still read by their chapter alone (read in the code): the trial's progress
  and its vote, a betrayal on offer, a Truth Bullet locked by a failed Analyze
  and the Traces tab's chapter filter, and, after a reset that clears the
  Remnants and keeps the Truth Bullets, the chapter a Key Remnant copy was
  found in. An autopsy or a silence recorded before
  1.2.73 has no season and counts as this chapter's until it ends (measured in
  tier 2).
- A console call to `game.drpg.setClock` with an Eclipse opens one past the
  hold; the guard sits in `startEclipse`, and nothing in the module makes that
  call (read in the code, not run).
- Not measured: whether Foundry fires `deleteToken` for the tokens of a
  deleted scene; whether the promotion window, opening after the
  toast, hides behind the card's chat. Whether a witness's position outside
  every room is legal is left to stage E12.

## Checked

- The headless suite, run as `npm test` on this release's code (commit
  a68175a: the tree that ships but for the version stamps, these notes, the
  stage registry's rows and the local gate's record): 1179 passed, 0 failed,
  17 skipped (1.2.72: 1114, 0 and 17). The scenarios: 21 of 21 green; 72's
  three expected reds stand (S17-31 until E43, a Foundry limit, S17-64 until
  E60). The lint, the checks and the gate's self-test were green in the same
  run. Its first run, on c954c64, was red on one check, scenario 33's B4b:
  the check compared two clock readings taken on either side of one socket
  read, and the module's order was right in all 200 sends measured. B4b now
  reads whether the request had answered at the moment the message is said
  (test only, a68175a), and the suite ran again.
- The Polish file's prose check on the stage's last commit (a68175a): 497 of
  497 strings covered.
- E11 had an independent review in two rounds (security and correctness), a
  goal check in each round, and an early review of each of its first seven
  commits as it landed. Their findings were fixed in the stage, 5 commits
  after the first round and 7 after the second; what the fixes left open is
  under Known gaps. The second round's fixes had no independent review of their
  own.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: the audit's live checks, section 9.2,
  items 154 to 162 (LIVE-E11-01 to 09). The local release gate needs a local
  Foundry v14 and did not run for this release.
